Age from CPR numbers

Source: R/cpr_vectors.R
cpr_age.Rd

The vector version of the age selection in add_cpr_info(): CPR numbers in, ages in completed calendar years out. It takes the same references as age(), but as values rather than column names, so it fits inside dplyr::mutate().

Usage

cpr_age(x, year, at = "primo", date, primo = "previous_ultimo")

Arguments

x

A vector of CPR numbers, cleaned as in clean_cpr().

year

Numeric whole year(s): one for all, or one per CPR number. Inside dplyr::mutate() this can be a column, e.g. cpr_age(pnr, year).

at, date, primo

As in age(): at is "primo", "medio" or "ultimo"; date is a Date vector or ISO date strings instead of year; primo is the convention for at = "primo".

Value

An integer vector of the same length as x.

Details

With neither year nor date, age is today's. Use an explicit reference for reproducible analysis. The default age(year) convention applies: primo is 31 December of the previous year, so opening ages equal the previous year's closing ages. See age() for the conventions and add_cpr_info() for leap-day birthdays.

Ages are NA for CPR numbers that are not valid (see cpr_valid()) and for missing references.

See also

age(), add_cpr_info(), cpr_birth_date()

Examples

x <- c("0101004007", "111111-1118", "3102004007")
cpr_age(x, 2025)
#> [1]  24 113  NA
cpr_age(x, 2025, "ultimo")
#> [1]  25 114  NA
cpr_age(x, date = "2025-07-01")
#> [1]  25 113  NA
cpr_age(x, year = c(2024, 2025, 2025))
#> [1]  23 113  NA

# df |> dplyr::mutate(alder = cpr_age(pnr, year))
